study.question: Observation: g3-r0003-embedding_item_primary improved click AUC from 0.6583679241 (joint) to 0.6601633627, while cart/fav/buy fell from 0.844383/0.863667/0.861406 to 0.679822/0.723578/0.662620. Context-only blocking preserved auxiliary AUCs but yielded click 0.6591803. Can nonzero, attenuated auxiliary gradients into shared item/action embeddings recover auxiliary predictiveness while preserving most of the primary-task gain, and does local ownership differ from globally reducing auxiliary loss weights?
study.hypothesis: Shared item geometry faces a strength-dependent tradeoff: eliminating auxiliary supervision protects click but deprives rare tasks of a useful representation. A fixed interior auxiliary item-gradient coefficient (0.1 or 0.5), with full auxiliary context, readout and tower training, can recover auxiliary information with less click harm than full joint training. This is an optimization intervention on a common forward representation, not evidence of conflicting individual examples or a new architecture. Local path scaling may differ from global loss weighting because non-item auxiliary learning remains unattenuated.

nearest_work.difference: STEM sections on embeddings and Eq.4 use shared plus task-specific embedding tables and detached other-task experts. Its author implementation detaches other-task expert outputs. Here one existing shared table is retained; only auxiliary target/value paths receive a fixed nonzero Jacobian. No STEM reproduction or priority claim; generic backward routing is inherited prior art.

Only the GradNorm primary abstract was read: it dynamically balances gradient magnitudes. This study uses fixed coefficients with no learned balancing, gradient norm measurement, optimizer replacement or GradNorm effectiveness claim. Static auxiliary BCE weighting is a simple replacement control, not a GradNorm reproduction.

INFNet exchanges categorical, sequence and task representations via proxy-guided interactions. No proxies or token interactions are newly adopted; task-specific local-activation rows are inherited. This study targets backward item supervision at fixed forward architecture.

inherited_components: The exact incumbent FeatureEmbeddingDict construction, user/item/action field detection and one shared embedding table
Target-conditioned DIN-style [q,k,q-k,q*k,action] interactions, masked before Dice; unnormalized task-specific score rows
Primary-owned selector trunk and auxiliary score-row learning on detached trunk hidden states
Four independent [128,64] Dice towers and the same reset/row-tying initialization order
All frozen host data, causal availability, official_offline history semantics, training recipe and validation metrics
study.proposed_difference: Replace hard detachment of auxiliary item embeddings by view g_a(x)=stopgrad(x)+a*(x-stopgrad(x)), with endpoint branches a=0 -> detach and a=1 -> identity. Apply before history-value pooling and to direct auxiliary target features, never after pooling: task score rows retain their ordinary gradients. Click and auxiliary context paths remain unchanged. Test a=0.1 and 0.5 with unit BCE weights. Include a=1 plus auxiliary BCE weight 0.1 and a=1 plus unit BCE weights. Every variant uses the same explicit sum-of-task-mean FP32 BCE hook; joint_hook_control diagnoses any deviation from the historical host loss. No additional trainable parameters or random draws.
predictions: At fixed initialized parameters all variants have identical forward probabilities, masking and parameter/state structure. For unweighted loss, changing a only multiplies auxiliary item/action embedding data gradients; click, context, selector readout and tower gradients remain unchanged. The existing primary selector prevents an auxiliary route through its trunk inputs.

Predeclared useful-tradeoff criterion (descriptive, not significance): at least one interior point has click AUC >= 0.6595, improves each auxiliary AUC over g3-r0003-embedding_item_primary by >= 0.05, and auxiliary mean AUC >= 0.82. Selection remains click validation AUC only; this diagnostic criterion does not redefine selection.

Compare local a=0.1 to aux_loss_010: at identical parameters their item embedding data gradients coincide, while context/readout/tower gradients differ. A subsequent performance difference supports a role for where attenuation is applied, with optimizer/clipping mediators retained explicitly.

Report all four AUC/Logloss values, auxiliary mean separately, history slices with sample/positive/negative counts, parameters, wall/GPU time, peak memory and latency/throughput where host receipts supply them. Expected parameter count is 32088328; cost must be measured, not inferred from equal parameters.
falsifiers: If joint_hook_control fails to reproduce historical joint predictions/metrics within numeric tolerance (AUC absolute 1e-6, Logloss 1e-6), do not attribute archived-endpoint differences to attenuation. Retain costs, investigate hook/source mismatch under a new plan.
If both interior points fail the predeclared useful-tradeoff criterion, reject this implementation as a demonstrated resolution; do not refute all task-conditioned representations.
If a weighted global-loss control matches or improves the local point on click and every auxiliary AUC at comparable measured cost, do not credit localization as necessary.

If changing a alters fixed-state forward probabilities, parameter counts, allowed inputs, or auxiliary score/tower gradients at unit loss weight, implementation validity fails before mechanism interpretation.
An ordering across two coefficients and one seed cannot establish monotonicity, gradient conflict, statistically reliable gains or generalization beyond the offline benchmark.
alternative_explanations: Prior improvement may reflect primary-prioritization at auxiliary expense rather than beneficial information exchange. Recovery of auxiliary AUC alone may simply restore joint training, losing click gains.

Adagrad per-coordinate normalization can make small auxiliary gradients effective where click gradients are weak; accumulated statistics can explain a sharp nonlinear response without a task-conflict mechanism.
Global loss scaling changes context and head optimization, AdamW effective regularization and dense clipping; these are part of the replacement intervention rather than isolated semantic transfer.
One-pass undertraining, rare-label imbalance, seed-dependent optimization, validation adaptation and Dice statistics can influence tradeoffs. No per-example gradient alignment is observed.

Auxiliary targets match user/category/brand over 24h rather than current-ad conversions; frozen offline delayed-feedback history and inherited vocab/static-snapshot assumptions limit deployment interpretation.
Private auxiliary embedding spaces could avoid the tradeoff more completely but add parameters; this cheaper path-strength diagnostic does not falsify that architectural alternative.

Thus the primary winner has a substantial multi-task tradeoff; adding context blocking was not a further primary improvement.
